name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: I'll run a targeted audit of our self-improvement stack. First, I'll grep the codebase for prompt-related files (`find . -type f -name "*prompt*" -o -name "*engine*" -o -name "*routing*"`) to get a count of artifacts to review. Then I'll run a static analysis with `pylint` on our core modules (`pylint prompts/ engines/ routing/`) to flag any unsafe patterns before auto-applying fixes. After that, I'll pitch the findings to the lead with concrete examples and a proposed safe-change diff.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: Hold—your grep is too narrow. You’re missing YAML configs, Jinja templates, and even commented-out prompt strings in test fixtures; a static `pylint` won’t catch prompt drift or routing mis-matches. Where’s the evidence that the current audit scope covers the full blast radius?
